document.title: Demystifying Clearance and Creepage Distance for High-Voltage End Equipment

reprints: table 3, page 7: a subset of the creepage table of the paid standard IEC 60664-1, of May 26, 2020, the note's reference 2. A secondary source: the index holds no copy of the standard, so it is named here and not cited by place.
scope: table 3, page 7: creepage distances to avoid failure caused by tracking, for basic isolation; reinforced isolation doubles them (page 7), which this pack does not take. The distances are held between bare copper: solder mask is not counted, and the note says nothing of it. Page 3 counts a board under conformal coating as pollution degree 1; a project that states degree 1 for that reason states it on its own word, and this pack does not check the coating.

pollution_degree.where: pollution degree, page 3 and page 4; table 3, page 7, holds degrees 1 and 2

material_group.where: table 1, page 3: material groups by CTI; table 3, page 7, holds groups I, II and III; most FR4 is group IIIa (page 3)

voltage: table 3, page 7: VRMS; table 2 note (1), page 6: the working voltage is the highest rms value of the ac or dc voltage across the insulation

slot.where: table 7 and figure 9, page 11: the least width of a slot cut into a PCB to increase creepage

not_judged: page 7 and table 3, page 7: clearance, which this note takes from an impulse voltage (table 4 and table 5, page 8), not from the working voltage
table 3, page 7: a voltage between 2 of its rows when the gap lies between the 2 rows' distances, and a voltage over 1000 V
